description: Search television news closed captions for spoken mentions of a query. Returns a bounded, paged per-station time series showing airtime devoted to the topic — 500 points by default, up to 20,000 per page. Each series carries GDELT's display name for the station and, when that name resolves to one, the station ID gdelt_get_tv_clips takes as stations. Use stations to select station IDs (e.g. ["CNN", "FOXNEWS", "MSNBC"]), or select with station:, network:, or quoted market: operators in query. TV query also supports in-query operators: station:CNN, network:CBS, market:"National", show:"Anderson Cooper 360", context:"vaccine". Archive coverage varies by station; use gdelt_list_tv_stations for station IDs, network and market values, and monitoring date ranges.

combined.description: Pool selected stations into one Combined timeline. Normalized values divide pooled matching clips by pooled monitored clips; false keeps separate station series.

dateres.description: Optional GDELT aggregation resolution. Omit to let GDELT choose from the window length — hourly up to 7 days, daily under 3 years, monthly beyond; the effective recognized or inferred resolution is returned as dateResolution. Each point counts one whole UTC period: a clock hour, day, Sunday–Saturday week, month, or year.

endDatetime.description: End datetime in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS — exactly 14 digits, no separators (e.g. 20200131235959). Must pair with startDatetime; supplying only one of the two is rejected. GDELT extends it through the end of its UTC period at the response resolution — an end exactly on the clock hour counts as the second before it, so it adds no period starting there; notice then names the window the values cover.

limit.description: Maximum timeline points returned per page (default 500, cap 20,000). Larger counts clamp with limitClamp; strict deployments reject them.

normalize.description: When true (default), values are normalized as % of total airtime, enabling cross-station comparison. When false, returns raw matching 15-second clip counts.

offset.description: Zero-based point offset into the deterministic date-then-station-name ordering. Use nextOffset from the preceding response with the same query inputs to retrieve the next page.

query.description: Search query for TV transcript content. Supports TV operators: station:CNN, network:CBS, market:"National", show:"Anderson Cooper", context:"vaccine". Boolean OR in parentheses ((flu OR pandemic)) and phrases also work.

smoothing.description: Trailing moving-average width in timesteps, 0–30 (0 or 1 = none). Width N needs N source steps; leading steps cannot produce averages and peaks may appear later.

startDatetime.description: Start datetime in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS — exactly 14 digits, no separators (e.g. 20200101000000). Must pair with endDatetime; supplying only one of the two is rejected. GDELT widens it back to the start of its UTC period at the response resolution; notice then names the window the values cover.

stations.description: Station IDs to filter to (e.g. ["CNN", "FOXNEWS", "MSNBC"]) — the stationId values gdelt_list_tv_stations returns, not display labels such as "FOX News". Every supplied ID is forwarded. Alternatively use station:, network:, or quoted market: selectors in query; a selector is required. Obtain network and market values and per-station archive ranges from gdelt_list_tv_stations.

timespan.description: Relative window counting back from now (a number and unit such as d, m, or y). Now is past the end of most stations' monitoring, so for archived periods set startDatetime/endDatetime inside a station's range from gdelt_list_tv_stations. Ignored when startDatetime/endDatetime are set.

name: gdelt_search_tv

combined.description: True for one pooled Combined timeline; false for separate station series.

dateResolution.description: Temporal resolution of data points — as GDELT reported it, as requested via dateres, or inferred from the returned intervals. Omitted when none of those can establish it.

effectiveQuery.description: The query the call ran, for use in follow-up calls: the query given or, when it only joins terms with OR outside parentheses, those terms as one group.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_date_range`: Only one of startDatetime / endDatetime was supplied, one of them is not a real UTC calendar timestamp, or startDatetime is not earlier than endDatetime. `offset_out_of_range`: The requested point offset is at or beyond the end of a non-empty timeline. `invalid_query`: A stations entry is not a station ID, the query has OR outside parentheses with no single reading, GDELT rejected the query — no station was selected, or the query string is malformed — or the TV timespan is malformed. `gdelt_rate_limited`: GDELT rejected the request for its one-request-per-five-seconds limit, or too many requests were already queued for this one to start in time. `gdelt_unavailable`: GDELT TV API is unreachable or temporarily returned no usable data. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

limit.description: Maximum points this page holds — the requested limit, or 20,000 when a larger one was clamped.

limitClamp.description: Present only when the requested count exceeded the per-call cap: the call ran exactly as a call at the cap, and every count, notice, and continuation in this response reflects the applied value.

applied.description: The per-call cap the call ran with instead.

parameter.description: The count input that was clamped.

requested.description: The value the call asked for.

nextOffset.description: Offset for the next page using the same query inputs. Absent when this is the final page.

normalized.description: True when values are normalized coverage percentages.

notice.description: When the query's terms were joined by OR outside parentheses, the grouped query that ran. When smoothing is above 1, that leading steps without a full window have no values and peaks may lag. When the query matched no TV coverage: the resolved timespan window; for each selected station whose monitoring range the window misses, that range and how to search inside it; and how to check station coverage. When an explicit startDatetime or endDatetime falls inside a UTC period of the response resolution: the resolution and the UTC window the values cover. When a returned series has no station ID, why: GDELT returned it without a station label, or its station catalog did not load or has no entry for the named label — with how to look the ID up. Absent when the query ran as given, coverage was returned, smoothing is at most 1, the window is a timespan or sits on period boundaries, and every series carries its station ID or combined is true.

offset.description: Zero-based offset of this point page.

series.description: Station series represented in this point page.

items.description: Coverage time series for a single station.

data.description: Time-ordered coverage data for this station on this page.

date.description: Label of the UTC period the point covers, in ISO 8601: the hour's start for hourly points, and 12:00:00Z of the period's first day for day, week, month, and year points.

value.description: Coverage value (normalized % or raw matching 15-second clip count).

peak.description: The point of the whole series with the largest absolute value, the earliest timestep on a tie, across every page — it may lie outside data.

date.description: Label of the UTC period the point covers, in ISO 8601: the hour's start for hourly points, and 12:00:00Z of the period's first day for day, week, month, and year points.

pointCount.description: Points in the whole series, across every page — not only those in data.

station.description: Station ID — the value the stations input and the station: operator take (e.g. "FOXNEWS"). Absent when GDELT's label for the station could not be resolved to an ID; notice says why.

stationName.description: GDELT's display label for the station (e.g. "FOX News"). Empty when GDELT returned the series without one; notice says so.

staleResponse.description: Present only when the refetch of this exact request was refused, failed, or came back empty, and the response is GDELT's stored answer from fetchedAt instead. It holds nothing published after fetchedAt; a relative timespan covers the window ending at fetchedAt, not now. Absent on a live answer.

ageSeconds.description: Age of the stored answer when served, in whole seconds.

fetchedAt.description: ISO 8601 time GDELT returned the stored answer.

reason.description: Why the refetch was not used: GDELT rate-limited it, did not answer with data, or answered empty — which GDELT also does under load.

timeRange.description: Date range spanned by this returned point page. Omitted when the page is empty.

end.description: Latest date in the returned data.

start.description: Earliest date in the returned data.

totalPoints.description: Total points available across all matched station series before pagination.

title: Search GDELT TV News
